**Claim:** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`domain:ui` execution seat) — branch `claude/issue-6310-dead-designer-formula-key`. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` in the same label write.

## Pre-dispatch gate

**1. Thread read.** Triage comment (18:07:53Z) read in full; its dispatch shape is the scope below.
**2. Shadow check.** Nothing in flight. Batch-mates: **#6396** (`components/renderers/form`) and **#6309** (`app-shell/.../previews`). Checked against the batch as well as the in-flight set — no overlap with `plugin-designer` or `packages/i18n/src/locales/`.
**3. Premise.** ⛔ Re-derive on the merged tree; `main` has moved many times since filing.

## Scope — measure the size of the job first

**Step 1: run `node scripts/check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs --strict`** to learn whether this key is one of a batch.

- **Backlog exists** ⇒ sweep the **whole verified-dead set in one commit**. ⛔ Each key **individually confirmed dead** — dynamic-construction false positives excluded **by hand**. The script's own header explains why it is report-only: a reverse sweep over dynamically constructed keys produces false positives. ⭐ **That is not a reason to distrust the tool; it is a reason the human step is mandatory.** Do not batch-delete its output.
- **No backlog** ⇒ just this key.

**Either way, the defaults map and all ten packs move together**, so `defaults-maps-mirror-en-pack` stays green:
- `packages/plugin-designer/src/hooks/useDesignerTranslation.ts` — `DESIGNER_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS`
- `packages/i18n/src/locales/{en,de,es,fr,pt,ru,ja,ko,zh,ar}.ts`

## ⚠️ The card's own fence — do not cross it

`designer.field.formula` (`'Formula (CEL)'`) is a **different, live** key belonging to metadata-admin's `ObjectFieldInspector`, the surface that still authors formula expressions. **Only the `appDesigner.fieldDesigner.*` spelling is dead.**

⭐ Two keys, both ending `.formula`, both about formulas, one live and one dead. A search for `formula` will hit both, and deleting the wrong one removes a working surface's label in ten languages. **Grep the full dotted path, not the leaf.**

## Tests

- `defaults-maps-mirror-en-pack` and the i18n parity gates are the real check — they are what catch a pack left behind. Run them and quote the verdicts.
- ⛔ **The ghost-assertion guard does not apply in its usual form** — a deletion adds no behaviour to pin. ⛔ Do not invent an assertion to satisfy the ritual; say so in the PR body. What replaces it: the **`--strict` output before and after**, and a positive control showing the tool still reports a key you know is live if you ask it to.
- If any test, snapshot or fixture references the key, that is a consumer the sweep missed — **stop and report**, ⛔ do not edit the test to make the deletion fit.

## Ground rules

Worktree-first: `git worktree add ../objectui-6310 -b claude/issue-6310-dead-designer-formula-key main && cd ../objectui-6310 && pnpm install`. ⛔ Never `git stash` — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Changeset: `patch`, per package changed. Open the PR as **draft** with `Fixes #6310` and report back — the PM lands it, ⛔ never self-merge.

If the sweep turns out to be much larger than one key, **report the size before landing a large deletion** — a ten-key sweep and a hundred-key sweep are different reviews.

Size: S (larger if the sweep is a batch — report first). Model: opus.

## PM review — **ACCEPT** (retirement + pin)

PR #6411, head `ccacdc43b`, two commits. `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session
`session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`. The pin I ruled for is on the branch; this is the review of
it, verified against the tree rather than read from the report.

### The pin does the one thing I was worried it would get wrong

My ruling came with a specific hazard attached: a `SURVIVING` list built from *the rows next to
the deleted one* would pin "these are live" against keys that are themselves unconfirmed
reverse-sweep candidates — trading a silent dead key for a guard that asserts something nobody
measured. The row immediately after the retired one is `options`, and it is one of those.

`SURVIVING` **excludes all eight** — `addOption`, `addRule`, `noFields`, `options`,
`searchPlaceholder`, `systemBadge`, `ungrouped`, `validationRules` — and the docblock says so in
writing, with the reason, so the exclusion can never be re-read as an oversight by someone
tidying up later. That is the part that makes this a guard rather than a ritual.

**Verified independently — every `SURVIVING` member has a real call site**, not just proximity
(`packages/plugin-designer/src/FieldDesigner.tsx`, counted on the branch):

```
referenceTo 1 · typeSpecificSection 1 · defaultValue 1 · placeholder 1
fieldType 2 · title 1 · allTypes 1
```

Seven for seven. Nothing in that list is there because it was nearby.

### The retirement itself, re-measured

`appDesigner.fieldDesigner.formula` at head: **zero occurrences across the ten packs.**
Positive control on the same pathspec — `referenceTo:` still declared in **10/10 packs** — so the
zero is a real zero and not a pathspec that stopped matching. The `DESIGNER_DEFAULT_TRANSLATIONS`
row went in the same commit, which is what keeps `defaults-maps-mirror-en-pack` and
`all-locales-key-parity` from reddening in opposite directions.

### The fourth case is an addition to the precedent, and a good one

The four prior retirement pins (#4145 / #4392 / #4730 / #5504) established RETIRED + SURVIVING +
non-vacuity. This one adds a case pinning the **dynamically built `typeCategory.*` family** —
six keys reached only through `` t(`appDesigner.fieldDesigner.typeCategory.${cat}`) `` at
`FieldDesigner.tsx:262`, confirmed live on the branch.

⭐ That is precisely the class a future literal-argument reverse sweep would mistake for dead:
no member is spelled at any call site, `all-locales-key-parity` is satisfied by all ten packs
dropping one together, and the failure mode is a raw key rendering in the type filter with every
gate green. Pinning them by name closes a hole none of the four precedents covered.

The non-vacuity case is real too — `LANGS` length 10 *and* a ≥20-key `appDesigner.fieldDesigner`
root, so the file cannot pass by iterating an empty pack list or by asserting absence inside a
namespace that itself vanished.

### The failure message earns its length

It names `designer.field.formula` (`'Formula (CEL)'`, metadata-admin's `ObjectFieldInspector`) as
the **live, different** key, so the next person to meet this guard meets both spellings at once
rather than concluding the repo has no formula label. Two keys end in `.formula`; only one is
retired. That distinction was the card's own fence and the pin now carries it.

### Landing

CI at `ccacdc43b`: 25 checks complete and green, 3 test shards still running, **0 failures**.
⛔ Not enqueued — 入队资格 is *every* check green, and it goes to the merge queue when the
shards land. ⭐ Worth stating plainly why the earlier all-green reading did **not** buy an
enqueue: `b1cf72cca` was 25 ✅ / 0 ❌ / `clean`, and it was still the wrong thing to land, because
that head predated the pin. Green measured against a head that is no longer the deliverable is
not evidence about the deliverable.

The backlog stays untouched and still tracked by #4730 — 389 candidates / 150 CONFIRMED /
239 NEEDS-REVIEW across 55 namespaces, which I have posted onto that card.
